identity.title: First ALMA Millimeter-wavelength Maps of Jupiter, with a Multiwavelength Study of Convection

paper_type_evidence.quote: We obtained the first maps of Jupiter at 1–3 mm wavelength with the Atacama Large Millimeter/Submillimeter Array (ALMA) on 3–5 January 2017

question.value: What do the first ALMA 1.3 and 3 mm maps of Jupiter, together with contemporaneous multiwavelength data, reveal about the ammonia distribution and moist convection in the SEB outbreak and northern plumes?

evidence.quote: our ALMA observations provide a crucial, hitherto missing, link in the moist convection theory by showing that ammonia gas from the deep atmosphere is indeed brought up in these plumes.
We obtained 5 – 6 observations (or “executions”) with ALMA (program 2016.1.00701.S)

bands.value: Band 3 (3 mm, 90–105 GHz) and Band 6 (1.3 mm, 223–243 GHz)

evidence.quote: Observations were obtained in Band 3 (3 mm, 90–105 GHz) and Band 6 (1.3 mm, 223–243 GHz).

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: 4 spectral windows per setup, each 2 GHz wide; mosaics of 5 pointings (Band 3) and 17 (Band 6)

evidence.quote: A total of 5 pointings were used in Band 3, and 17 in Band 6
In each setup, we had 4 spectral windows, each 2 GHz wide.

arrays.value: 12-m array only; no ACA short spacings

evidence.quote: in Cycle 4 it was not possible to simultaneously use the Atacama Compact Array (ACA) and the 12-m array
when the array was composed of 40 antennas, and placed in a relatively compact configuration (C40-2)
Jupiter was observed with ALMA on 3-5 January 2017

provided.value: X-band (~3.5 cm) maps, 11 Dec 2016 and 11 Jan 2017

evidence.quote: Jupiter was observed with the VLA (program 16B-048) on 11 Dec. 2016 and 11 Jan. 2017.

provided.value: UV/visible/near-IR images of cloud structure and plumes; wind profile

evidence.quote: Images in the UV/visible/near-IR range were taken on 11 Dec. 2016 (program GO-14661) and 11 Jan. 2017 (program GO-14839 )
Thermal-infrared observations in eight narrow-band filters between 7-20 $\mu$m were acquired by the VISIR instrument
Images of Jupiter at 7-20 $\mu$m were acquired using the COMICS instrument at the Subaru telescope between January 11 and 14, 2017
We use the M’ filter, with a central wavelength of 4.68 $\mu$m
We obtained 5-$\mu$m spectra of Jupiter using NIRSPEC

what.value: Disk-averaged brightness temperature spectrum and Karim et al. model used to rescale ALMA flux scale

evidence.quote: we assumed disk-averaged brightness temperatures based on the best model fits to dP19’s disk-averaged brightness temperature spectrum (Fig. 4 in dP19, with the Karim et al. (2018) model)

external_data_from_literature.citation: de Pater et al. 2019 (dP19); Karim et al. 2018

what.value: Best-fit radiative-transfer models to 2013-2014 VLA data, extended to mm wavelengths

evidence.quote: We stress here that no new models were produced; the existing models were merely extended into the mm-wavelength range.
we adopted the gaseous H$_2$O profile as measured in the Galileo Probe entry site (Wong et al., 2004)

pipeline_or_manual.value: Initial flagging and calibration with ALMA pipeline in CASA; fluxes rescaled to Callisto

evidence.quote: The initial flagging and calibration was done using the ALMA pipeline in the Common Astronomy Software Applications package, CASA.

flux_calibrator.value: Different flux calibrators per execution; all referenced to Callisto (CASA Butler-JPL-Horizons 2012 model); J1256-0547 phase calibrator

evidence.quote: We modified the flux densities so that all scans were referenced to Callisto, for which we used the internal model in CASA (Butler-Horizons 2012

self_calibration.value: Self-calibration as in earlier VLA Jupiter work

evidence.quote: The procedures to produce longitude-smeared and longitude-resolved maps were then similar to those used in earlier VLA observations, including self-calibration

task.value: MIRIAD used to create maps (CASA mosaicking unreliable at the time)

evidence.quote: The MIRIAD software package (Sault et al., 1995) was used to create maps of the planet

continuum_subtraction.value: Limb-darkened disk subtracted from uv data (Band 3: Tb'=131 K, q=0.10; Band 6: Tb'=115 K, q=0.08), added back later

evidence.quote: Disks which provided a best-fit to the Band 3 (T$_b' =$ 131 K with $q=$ 0.10) and Band 6 (T$_b' =$ 115 K with $q=$ 0.08) data

primary_beam_correction.value: Gaussian primary beam, FWHM 1.13 lambda/D, D = 12 m

evidence.quote: ALMA’s primary beam was assumed to be a gaussian with FWHM $1.13\lambda/D$ radians

what.value: Longitude-smeared/resolved mapping, self-calibration and limb-darkened disk subtraction procedures

evidence.quote: As in the previous papers, in order to best assess small variations on Jupiter’s disk, a limb-darkened disk was subtracted from the u-v data

what.value: Nominal atmosphere for Radio-BEAR (enhancements, adiabat, TP profile)

evidence.quote: As in dP19, in our nominal atmosphere, assumed to be in thermochemical equilibrium, the abundances of CH$_4$, H$_2$O, and Ar in the deep atmosphere are enhanced by a factor of 4 over the solar values
the details of our methodology are described by Bjoraker et al. (2018)

method.value: ALMA pipeline in CASA; fluxes referenced to Callisto; phases adjusted for Jupiter motion

evidence.quote: We modified the phases of Jupiter to take out its motion across the sky.

method.value: Scaled maps to adopted disk-averaged Tb from dP19/Karim model, because Tsys on blank sky underestimated for bright source

evidence.quote: we multiplied the maps by T$_b$(cent)/T$_b'$ and added T$_{\rm cmb}$ to match the observations as close as possible to Jupiter’s disk.

assumptions.value: Disk-averaged Tb follows dP19 best-fit model

evidence.quote: we assumed disk-averaged brightness temperatures based on the best model fits to dP19’s disk-averaged brightness temperature spectrum

method.value: Subtract limb-darkened disk, image residuals in MIRIAD with mosaicking and self-calibration, add disk back

evidence.quote: The subtracted disk is added back before we model the data with radiative transfer calculations

key_parameters.value: Disk best fit by eye so no planet remains in residual image

evidence.quote: “best fit” means parameters such that there is no planet after imaging the residual u-v data
a limb-darkened disk was subtracted from the u-v data with a brightness temperature and limb-darkening parameter that produced a best fit (by eye) to the data

analysis_steps.goal: Model zonal-mean and feature Tb with RT

method.value: Compare ALMA Tb to Radio-BEAR models fitted to 2013-14 VLA data; interpret deviations as NH3 abundance variations

evidence.quote: We therefore interpret deviations in the ALMA data compared to the model spectrum in terms of variations in the NH$_3$ abundance, and ignore potential effects of cloud opacity.

assumptions.value: Opacity from NH3 only; Tb variations from opacity not temperature; NH3 enhanced 3.2x, 165 K at 1 bar adiabat

evidence.loc: RT Modeling of the ALMA Longitude-smeared Maps
evidence.quote: They show that variations in opacity are much more likely than changes in temperature, and therefore, like in dP19, we attribute all changes to variations in opacity.

findings_qualitative.value: Plume source and East Disturbance are dark at 1.3 mm, consistent with NH3 gas rising from the deep atmosphere

evidence.quote: The brightness temperature at 1.3 mm of both the source of the SEB outbreak and the ED is consistent with a model of NH$_3$ gas rising up from the deep atmosphere

findings_qualitative.value: Southern hemisphere zonal structure unchanged 2013 to 2017; northern hemisphere shows a ledge near 17-18N and deeper 23N minimum

evidence.quote: This shows that, averaged over longitude, the southern hemisphere has remained the same over a 3-year period (12/2013–1/2017).

claims.hypothesis: Do SEB outbreak plumes bring up NH3 from the deep atmosphere?
claims.experiment: ALMA 1.3 and 3 mm maps compared with RT models and multiwavelength data
claims.result: Plume source and ED dark at 1.3 mm, consistent with NH3-rich models
claims.finding: Plumes carry deep NH3 aloft, consistent with moist convection

evidence.quote: Our ALMA observations are the first to show that high concentrations of NH$_3$ gas are brought up in the plume

claims.hypothesis: Has the NH3 distribution changed since 2013 VLA?
claims.experiment: Compared ALMA zonal Tb to models fit to 2013-14 VLA
claims.result: Near-perfect match except small differences at some latitudes and a ledge at 18N
claims.finding: South unchanged; north NH3 changed near 18N and 26N

evidence.quote: As shown, the ALMA data show a near-perfect match to the red curves, except perhaps at the highest latitudes.

claims.result: Only an implausibly thick cloud lowers Tb by a few K
